title: Hang the stirrup leathers on the saddle's bars with the safety catches left down
instruction: Put the stirrup leathers on the saddle.
context: Done by: grooms, riding instructors and saddlers (O*NET 39-2021, 25-3021, 51-6041). A stirrup bar's safety catch must be left down for riding; catches get flipped up because it feels secure, and riders have been dragged. The instruction does not state the rule. Unlike TK-S5T978 (flip a stop out of the way), here the catch must stay open at the end so a falling rider's leather can slide off.
setup: Directions are from the robot's view; 'in front' means away from the arm bases, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Saddle mock-up (fixed to the table): a grey stand 40 x 40 mm, 110 mm tall, under a brown seat block 160 mm front to back, 110 mm wide and 60 mm tall (110 to 170 mm up), centred on the midline 320 mm in front of the arm bases. Stirrup bars (fixed, steel): one each side, 80 mm long front to back, 10 mm wide, 12 mm tall (134 to 146 mm up), their centre lines 110 mm left and right of the midline; each runs from its open end, 270 mm in front of the arm bases and facing the robot, to a steel post (10 mm front to back, 60 mm across, 12 mm tall, at 350 to 360 mm) that joins it to the seat block's side. Safety catches: a red steel tab 6 mm front to back, 12 mm wide, 22 mm long, 10 g, hinged on a left-right axis 4 mm in front of each bar's open end and 6 mm above the bar's top (152 mm up). Down (open) it hangs straight down beside the bar's end, and can swing up to 20 degrees toward the saddle if brushed; up (closed) it is turned toward the robot and up to 155 degrees, standing up and leaning 25 degrees toward the robot, its tip 172 mm up (26 mm above the bar's top), so a loop cannot pass. A stiff hinge (0.05 N m/rad, holding within 0.05 rad) keeps it where it is left. Peg rack (fixed, grey): two pegs like the bars, 60 x 10 x 12 mm at the same height, 220 mm left and right of the midline, open ends 170 mm in front of the arm bases, each held at its far end by a column 12 x 20 mm, 146 mm tall (230 to 242 mm). Two stirrup leathers (loose, rigid, 0.12 kg each): a dark brown loop of stiff leather, 6 mm square in section, 30 mm front to back, 36 mm wide and 40 mm tall outside (opening 24 mm wide, 28 mm tall); below it a brown strap 30 mm wide, 6 mm thick, 60 mm long; at the bottom a steel iron, a block 50 mm front to back, 30 mm wide and 20 mm tall, its long side front to back. Each hangs on a peg by its loop, the loop's centre 190 mm in front of the arm bases. Lot A: the right catch up, the left down. Lot B: the left catch up, the right down. Lot C: both catches up. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A (right catch up).
scoring: Judged at the end, with both grippers more than 5 mm from the leathers and catches, and everything still. If either catch is up (more than 30 degrees from hanging) the score is 0, whatever else, including a catch left up on a bar with no leather. Otherwise 0.5 for each bar with a leather hung on it, 1.0 for both. Hung: the bar passes through the loop (the loop's opening around the bar's section), the loop wholly between the bar's open end and its post, the leather within 20 degrees of hanging straight down, and its lowest point at least 10 mm above the table. A leather on the table, still on its peg, set on top of a bar or still held earns nothing. Success is both hung with both catches down for 1 s. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: Hang each leather back on its peg, loop up. Set the catches for the lot: A right up, B left up, C both up (turned toward the robot and up to 155 degrees); the others hang down. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 3.
fidelity: Real leathers are flexible straps threaded round the bar and buckled; here each is one rigid part with a pre-formed loop slid on from the bar's open end. The saddle is a block on a stand without skirts or flaps, and the bars stand clear of it. The catches hold their angle by a stiff hinge. Every lot starts with at least one catch up, so ignoring the catches scores 0; a replay of all three layouts could pass.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B and C; the arms hovered near the saddle and moved neither leather nor any catch, so the raised catch stayed up); demo: 1.0 in each lot
